opportunities.name: Open-source project lead research (HN + GitHub → Notes)
opportunities.description: For a given open-source project, find its top Hacker News story (points, age) and its GitHub repo stats (stars, latest release date), then add a 'Lead:' entry in the Notes app.
steps: Open Hacker News search (hn.algolia.com) and search for {project}
Record the top story title, points and age
Open github.com and search for {project} in the header search
Open the top repository result and read the star count and latest release date
Open the Notes app and add a new note: 'Lead: {project}. HN "{title}" ({points} pts, {age}); GitHub {stars} stars, last release {date}'

instances.values: project=llama.cpp (HN 1311 pts, GitHub 131.1k stars, release Oct 5 2026)
project=Zed (HN 'Zed 1.0' 2153 pts, GitHub 91.7k stars, release Oct 12 2026)
project=Bun (HN 2192 pts, GitHub 96.2k stars, release Oct 10 2026)

opportunities.name: Company court-case pitch (CourtListener + Wikipedia → email)
opportunities.description: For a given company, find a notable court opinion on CourtListener, check company facts (HQ, CEO) on Wikipedia, and email a story pitch to lena@example.com.
steps: Open courtlistener.com and search case law for {company}
Open the top relevant opinion and note the case name, court and filing date
Read the headquarters and CEO from the article infobox
Open New message, set To to lena@example.com
Write a body that cites the case, court, filing date, HQ and CEO, and ask whether it's worth a piece

instances.values: company=Uber (Uber v. Uber, Ohio Ct. App., Mar 31 2017; HQ San Francisco, CEO Dara Khosrowshahi), sent to lena@example.com
company=Airbnb (CourtListener search, 412 opinions; no email seen)
company=Tesla (CourtListener search attempted; Wikipedia Tesla page; no email seen)

opportunities.name: Country fact-check (World Bank indicator + BBC context → Notes)
opportunities.description: For a given country, look up its life expectancy on World Bank Open Data, find a recent BBC News story on the country, and save a 'Fact-check' note.
steps: Open data.worldbank.org and type {country} in the search box
Select the country to open its economy page
Read life expectancy at birth (value and year)
Open bbc.com, open the menu search and search '{country} {topic}'
Open or read the top result headline and its age
Open the Notes app and add: 'Fact-check {country}: Life expectancy at birth {value} ({year}). Context: {headline} ({age})'

instances.values: country=Kenya, topic=health (life expectancy 64 in 2024; BBC Ebola quarantine story)
country=Vietnam, topic=climate (Viet Nam 75 vs Kenya 64; BBC 'Why Vietnam's coffee beans might outlast others'); no note seen
country=Argentina (World Bank search only; search did not resolve, no BBC step seen)
